text:
Kaapo Kakko has 13 points in 16 games for Seattle, ten of them assists, and Yahoo Sports wondered this month whether the Rangers regret trading him. The Kraken are about to take him home: NHL.com's Tom Gulitti wrote about his excitement for the Global Series in Helsinki, quoting him: "I've been waiting the whole season to get there."

On the ice, the passing is genuine. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups coming from behind the net last season, more than double a typical forward, and 67% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.7 wins above replacement, 73rd among forwards, while playing with weak teammates.

The points this season are inflated, though. Seattle has scored 7.1 more goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, and the 5v5 share is just 46% of expected goals. He also shoots rarely (14 shots). His points per 60 are above the top of his usual range, so expect the pace to drift down even if the role stays the same.
headline: Kakko's assists are real, the bounces less so
